idiom_name: one function per request over a sqlite3/libpq handle with explicit BEGIN/COMMIT
implementation_notes: C has no class layer to replace: the transaction script is simply a function that takes the request data and a database handle, runs its statements with sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_step (or libpq's PQexecParams) and brackets them with BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT or sqlite3_exec(). Keep the script in its own translation unit with a prototype in a header, and keep presentation (HTTP parsing, printf) out of it - the C API of the database is the thin gateway. The classic class-per-script structure is unnecessary here; when a script must be selected at runtime, a table of {name, function pointer} entries is the C equivalent of the Command-style variant. The manual BEGIN/COMMIT pair is the normal form, not a workaround, because the language offers no scope-exit hook to automate it.
pitfalls: Every early return between BEGIN and COMMIT that skips the rollback leaves the connection with an open transaction.
SQL assembled by string concatenation inside a hand-written script is the classic injection site; bind parameters with sqlite3_bind_* or use PQexecParams.
A single sqlite3 handle shared between threads needs its own mutex or one connection per thread - the handle is not thread-safe by default.
